plainLanguageNotice: Talking in TTI Discord is not consent to sell your messages or knowledge.
Mentioning the TTI Knowledge Broker bot in your own message asks TTI to DM you a private contribution-offer link; the mention is not the contribution, license, or sale.
The broker keeps only the Discord account and message pointer needed to open and audit that session. It does not copy the Discord message into TTI's sale corpus.
A sale-eligible contribution begins only when you deliberately submit it through TTI's own contribution intake and select a license scope.
You keep ownership of your contribution. The selected license lets TTI store, transform, provenance, correct, and—only for a Union-licensed scope—sublicense bounded derived knowledge products.
A Discord account may be linked privately for authentication and credit notices, but Union products use only your chosen attribution mode.
Credits are non-transferable ledger claims, not cash, securities, deposits, or settled wages; payout terms are not potential until separately reviewed and accepted.
You may stop future uses. Already settled customer licenses and required accounting records are not automatically erased; unpublished and unsold uses must stop after a valid revocation is admitted.
Corrections and disputes propagate through the provenance graph so buyers can learn that knowledge changed or was withdrawn.
prohibitedContribution: knowledge copied from another person's Discord message
material the contributor does not have authority to license

revocation.settledLicenses: continue under their frozen terms unless the buyer contract says otherwise

appeal.weight: Contributor may challenge attribution weights before sale or during the disclosed settlement window.
appeal.provenance: Contributor may challenge identity, scope, transformation, or omission.
appeal.decisionAuthority: Human TTI authority; automated systems may assemble evidence but may not finally adjudicate ownership or sensitive disputes.

sources.title: Discord Terms of Service
sources.relevance: Users retain their content; other people's content requires consent; Discord restricts commercializing content or data obtained from the service.

sources.title: Discord Developer Policy
sources.relevance: API Data may not be sold, licensed, commercialized, mined, or scraped; API message content may not train AI without Discord express permission.

sources.title: FTC Consumer Privacy
sources.relevance: Privacy representations must accurately disclose data use and be honored.
